source_text:
Decedis, inquit Caecilius, officio iudicis religiosi: nam periniurium est uires te actionis meae intergressu grauissimae disputationis infringere, cum Octauius integra et inlibata debeat singula, si potest, refutare.
Id quod criminaris, inquam, in commune, nisi fallor, conpendium protuli, ut examine scrupuloso nostram sententiam non eloquentiae tumore, sed rerum ipsarum soliditate libremus, necauocanda, quod quereris, diutius intentio, cum toto silentio liceat responsionem Ianuari nostri iam gestientis audire.
thought_title: Caecilius protests the judge's interruption; Marcus explains the shared shortcut
orientation: Caecilius has just finished his attack on Christianity, and Marcus the narrator, acting as judge, has proposed weighing the arguments carefully; Caecilius now objects that Marcus is cutting short his case before Octavius has answered each point.
pass_a_gloss: You are departing, Caecilius said, from the duty of a conscientious judge: for it is a great injustice that you break the strength of my case by the interruption of a very serious debate, when Octavius ought to refute each point, if he can, whole and undamaged. That which you accuse, I said, I have put forward, unless I am mistaken, as a shared shortcut, so that by a scrupulous examination we may weigh our opinion not by swelling of eloquence but by the solidity of the things themselves, and the attention which you complain about must not be called away any longer, since with total silence it is permitted to hear the response of our Januarius, who is already eager.

choices.english: the duty of a conscientious judge
choices.why: religiosus here means scrupulous or conscientious in duty, not 'religious' in the modern sense; the glossary's religio is not directly in play
rejected: the duty of a religious judge
the office of a pious judge

choices.why: the prefix per- intensifies iniuria; 'great injustice' keeps the legal register of the debate

choices.english: by the interruption of a very serious debate
choices.why: intergressus is a rare noun for stepping between; 'interruption' captures the act of cutting in
rejected: by the intervention of a most weighty dispute
by the interposition of a very grave discussion

choices.why: conpendium means a saving or shortcut; 'shared' renders in commune as benefiting both sides

choices.term: non eloquentiae tumore, sed rerum ipsarum soliditate
choices.english: not by swelling of eloquence but by the solidity of the things themselves
choices.why: tumor is literally swelling, a standard metaphor for inflated speech; soliditas is the concrete firmness of facts
rejected: not by the bombast of eloquence but by the solidity of the matters themselves
not by rhetorical inflation but by the substance of the facts

choices.why: Ianuarius is Octavius's other name; 'our' keeps the affectionate possessive of the narrator

pass_b_english: "You are abandoning the duty of a conscientious judge," Caecilius said, "for it is a great injustice to break the strength of my case by the interruption of a very serious debate, since Octavius ought to refute each point whole and undamaged, if he can."

"What you criticize," I said, "I have offered, unless I am mistaken, as a shared shortcut, so that by careful examination we may weigh our judgment not by swelling of eloquence but by the solidity of the things themselves. And the attention you complain about need not be diverted any longer, since in complete silence we may hear the response of our Januarius, who is already eager to speak."

last_rejected.why: ‘conpendium’ means a common compromise or common ground, not a ‘shortcut’.
last_rejected.ruling: 'Conpendium' (compendium) means shortcut/abridgment; 'shared' misreads 'in commune' (for common benefit/general advantage), but 'shortcut' is correct.
